{'text': 'When Apple finally responded to soaring memory and other component costs, its stance was anything but mild. Some models saw price hikes of more than 50%, while upgrades to memory and storage on certain configurations nearly doubled in price.', 'quality': 'good'}

{'text': 'These higher prices are expected to persist for years, and may even become a permanent fixture...', 'quality': 'good'}

{'text': '9to5Mac readers have long been skeptical about whether Apple will reduce prices once component shortages ease. More than two-thirds of respondents said they expect these price increases to be permanent.', 'quality': 'good'}

{'text': 'Subsequently, analyst reports indicated that supply chain prices will not see significant improvement before 2028, and even if conditions ease by then, any reductions will be quite limited. The current high pricing policy appears set to continue for at least several years, and may possibly never return to previous levels.', 'quality': 'good'}

{'text': 'If this turns out to be the case, how would you respond? Would you grit your teeth and continue purchasing Apple products at the same frequency? Or would you cut back on the number or frequency of purchases? Alternatively, would you take other approaches, such as opting for cheaper models, buying refurbished units, or waiting for price drops before making a purchase?', 'quality': 'good'}

{'text': 'Take part in our poll and share your thoughts in the comments section. The poll offers multiple options, allowing you to indicate several changes to your purchasing habits all at once.', 'quality': 'good'}
